results.evidence: Two independent trail descriptions put Granite Pass at 6,270 ft and 6,300 ft, and a third lists 6,300 ft; the pass sits about 1.25 mi and several hundred feet below Cutthroat Pass. The 6,600 ft in the approach prose was a copy of the Cutthroat Pass figure.

Sources split: one club route page says the line should never exceed class 3 and the classic guide calls it class 3 (one commenter reads that as 10-15 ft of low fifth class); a scramble blog rates it class 3/4 and a trip report hit a wet class 4 slab while admitting it was off the easiest line. No two sources give a 5.4 crux, and none settle whether the hardest move is class 3, 4 or low fifth, so no patch.

One hiking-association page gives 23.0 mi round trip to Snowy Lakes; two independent trip write-ups give 20 mi and 20-22 mi. The row's itinerary (23 mi) agrees; the partner-requirements 11-13 mi is roughly the one-way figure.

results.fact: Whether the Snowy Lakes spur is signed
results.evidence: Three independent write-ups call the spur unmarked or not well marked (look for a boot path); one hiking-association page calls it signed. The row's waypoint and watch_out (unsigned) match the majority; the only outlier is bivy[1].notes, which is owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch.

results.correct_value: No water at Cutthroat Pass; fill up at the last stream below it (Porcupine Creek area)
results.evidence: The PCT association trip page says there is no water at the pass and to fill up at Porcupine Creek below it; a hiking-association page describes 'a dry Cutthroat Pass'; a PCT section description names the Porcupine Creek crossing as the fill-up. The approach prose telling parties to top off at the pass is wrong.

results.correct_value: No overnight/wilderness permit required to camp at Snowy Lakes; Northwest Forest Pass to park
results.evidence: A backpacking guide states no overnight permit is needed (Northwest Forest Pass for parking); a club backpack listing says the same; a climbing blog says no backcountry permit is needed since the peak is outside the national park. The route stays on national forest outside designated wilderness, so the self-issue wilderness permit claims in access.permit and the trailhead waypoint are the outliers.

results.evidence: summitTimeHrs (10) equals the whole day-2 section (climb plus hike-out), while the schedule reaches the summit about 3-3.5 h from camp. No outside source giving a camp-to-summit time for this route was found, so the value is left for the null-not-compute class repair.

The USGS topo name point at the row's own Cutthroat Pass coordinate reads about 6,834 ft; a hiking-association page and an independent trip report both give 6,800 ft. The row's 6,600 ft (waypoint, approach, approach variant) disagrees with its own bivy entry (6,800) and with these sources.
